stem:
Meher looks at the diagram of quadrilateral $ABCD$. All four sides carry the same tick mark. No right-angle mark is shown.

Which claim correctly classifies $ABCD$?

options.text: $ABCD$ is a rhombus and a parallelogram; it is not a square because no right angle is shown.
Call $ABCD$ a rhombus while the four sides are allowed to be unequal.
Being a parallelogram is what creates the four equal side lengths.
Call $ABCD$ a square under the same marks, with right angles that are not shown.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal sides make a rhombus, and every rhombus is a parallelogram. A square also needs right angles, which are not marked. Dropping equal sides, reversing cause, or stretching to square all miss the classification.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source rhombus sides as quadrilateral ABCD with equal-side ticks and no right-angle marks.
